title: Swahili Coast Fish Tamarind
community: Swahili coast — the coastal tamarind fish
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Swahili Coast Fish Tamarind — whole fish or thick steaks pan-fried golden, then coated in a thick tamarind-coconut-spice glaze and finished in the pan. The definitive Swahili coast tamarind fish — bolder, stickier, and more dramatically flavoured than the plain tamarind version.
longDesc: This is the more assertive cousin of samaki wa ukwaju — the whole fish pan-fried first for a crispy exterior, then coated in a thick, sticky tamarind-coconut glaze that caramelises in the pan. The result is intensely flavoured and texturally extraordinary.
ingredients: 2 whole fish or 4 thick fish steaks — scored
// Marinade: 2 tbsp lemon, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt
steps: Marinate scored fish in lemon, turmeric, salt for 15 minutes.
Pan-fry fish in oil over medium-high heat — 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Remove fish. Pour glaze into the same hot pan.
Return fish. Coat in glaze. Cook 2 minutes each side — glaze caramelises.
chefTips: The pan-fry first, then glaze — this sequence is everything.
Let the glaze caramelise — do not stir the fish around.
commonMistakes: Glazing before frying — no crispy base.
cookingScience: See TZA071 for the initial fish sear science. The tamarind-honey glaze caramelises during the final pan cooking — tartaric acid from tamarind partially inverts the sucrose in honey to fructose and glucose, which caramelise at a lower temperature than sucrose alone. This is why tamarind-honey glazes brown faster than plain honey glazes.
sustainabilityTips: Indian Ocean fish from local coastal fishermen.
culturalNote: Swahili coast tamarind fish is the bold expression of the Zanzibar flavour palette — sour, sweet, spiced, and sticky, it is a fish preparation of uncommon intensity.
